strings: In the bustling town of Thelsamar, cook Vidra Hearthstove keeps the local laborers and miners fed with a famous highland staple: blood sausages. Preparing this hearty dwarven fare requires freshly gathered ingredients from the surrounding valley of Loch Modan.

Thelsamar is never short on hungry appetites. Between energetic children and weary miners returning from the Ironband Excavation, Vidra Hearthstove works tirelessly over the tavern stove. To keep the populace fed and satisfied, she relies on a local culinary tradition known across Loch Modan: savory blood sausages made from the wildlife wandering the rugged mountain pass.

While traditional blood sausage relies on fresh blood, seasoned meat, and natural casings, Vidra's recipe reflects the rugged pragmatism of the dwarves. Boar intestines provide the casings, bear meat forms the dense filling, and spider ichor is added to lend a sharp, pungent bite. Though collecting venomous fluid and entrails is not for the faint of heart, the result is a regional favorite that travelers quickly learn to appreciate.

Vidra Hearthstove is the resident cook and homemaker in Thelsamar, located within the Stoutlager Inn. She takes immense pride in feeding the hardworking folk of Loch Modan, especially the laborers from nearby excavation sites.
vidra | who is vidra | thelsamar cook
Why does the recipe use spider ichor?

Vidra uses spider ichor as a distinctive spice to give her blood sausages their signature kick. Dwarven palates are famously hardy, and the venomous fluid lends a pungent flavor that plain herbs cannot match.
spider ichor in sausage | why spider ichor | spider spice
The sausages feed the local townspeople, rambunctious children, and the weary workers returning each evening from grueling shifts at the Ironband Excavation site.
who eats blood sausage | why make sausage
All three components—black bears, mountain boars, and wood lurker spiders—roam the wilderness and wooded hills surrounding the lake across Loch Modan.
where to get bear meat | where to get boar intestines | ingredient locations
What casing is used for the sausages?
Vidra uses natural casings cleaned from local mountain boars, creating a sturdy shell capable of holding the dense bear meat and seasoned fillings intact over the fire.
sausage casings | boar intestines | casing recipe

Yes. If an adventurer brings Vidra the ingredients, she happily shares her recipe, allowing travelers with culinary skills to craft the hearty dwarven dish on their own.

Supplying Vidra helps keep Thelsamar's local workforce nourished as they maintain key infrastructure and excavate ancient ruins across Loch Modan.
Gathering ingredients for Vidra rewards aspiring chefs with the authentic recipe for Blood Sausage, expanding their repertoire of hearty field rations.
Blood sausage is a quintessential dwarven comfort food, embodying the rugged culinary tastes of Khaz Modan's mountain clans.

Thelsamar is bustling with hungry locals, from rowdy children running through the streets to exhausted laborers returning from the nearby excavation site. Vidra takes immense pride in keeping everyone fed with the town's famous blood sausages, but keeping up with that endless demand requires a steady supply of fresh local game.

Bear meat provides the hearty, filling core of Thelsamar's signature blood sausages. Loch Modan's bears roam plentifully in the surrounding wilderness, offering dense, rich meat capable of satisfying the demanding appetites of hardworking dwarven miners and laborers.

Vidra runs a busy kitchen and expects everyone in town to pull their weight. As she sees it, even visiting adventurers must earn their keep rather than expecting an easy handout, making hunting wild game in the hills a fair trade for a taste of her famous cooking.

Pilot Hammerfoot fears the worst for his comrade, Mori Hildelve, who ventured into the craggy hills of Dun Morogh on foot after wrecking his siege engine. Hildelve was searching for a rare ore vital for potent blastpowder, but days have passed amidst unsettling roars echoing through the peaks.

Dwarven siege engines are formidable war machines, but even iron treads struggle against the treacherous, jagged ridges of Dun Morogh. While scouring the slopes for a rare mineral deposit required to produce high-grade blastpowder, Pilot Mori Hildelve pushed his engine too far up a steep hill and busted the machine. Undeterred by the breakdown, Hildelve ordered his companion, Pilot Hammerfoot, to stay behind and guard the broken machinery while he pressed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot.

Days went by with no sign of Hildelve returning to camp. In the dead of night, strange and vicious beastly growls began echoing down from the rocky crags, turning Hammerfoot's mild impatience into creeping dread. Though Hildelve had a reputation for being as tough as nails, surviving the frigid heights of Dun Morogh without mechanized armor or heavy support against prowling predators is a dangerous gamble.

Following Hildelve's path up the slopes leads not to a stranded scout, but to a frozen tragedy. The dwarf's remains lie exposed to the elements, mauled and stripped by mountain scavengers. Clutched tightly in his lifeless hand are his roughly scribbled notes—and still draped over his ruined frame is his brigadier's vest, confirming that the brave siege engineer met an untimely and violent end.
Why was Pilot Hildelve out in the wilderness alone?

Hildelve was searching for a rare type of ore needed to craft high-grade dwarven blastpowder. When his siege engine broke down on a steep mountain slope, he chose to press on into the crags on foot rather than abandon the prospect.

Mori set off on foot days ago after wrecking his engine, leaving Hammerfoot behind. This errand completes a scouting line out of Coldridge Valley, carrying Grelin Whitebeard's completed report through the trogg-infested pass to his brother Senir in Kharanos. It bridges the secluded training grounds of Anvilmar with the broader troubles facing Dun Morogh. Through Senir's candid reception, travelers catch their first glimpse of political friction simmering between field scouts and the Ironforge Senate.

After Grelin Whitebeard recovers his stolen journal from the Frostmane trolls, he prepares a detailed report of the valley's threats for his brother Senir. Mountaineer Thalos, stationed guarding the gate out of Coldridge Valley, entrusts passing adventurers with carrying this dispatch. Leaving the relative seclusion of the introductory vale means braving the tunnel cut through the mountain, which has recently been overrun by violent troggs ambushing all traffic. Travelers who punch through emerge onto the snowblown highways of central Dun Morogh, following the main road straight into the cozy hub of Kharanos.
A Grumpy Welcome and Senate Politics

Senir Whitebeard, found seeking warmth over drinks at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, greets newcomers with rough mountaineer hospitality. Reading through Grelin's findings, Senir chuckles over his brother's aggressive rhetoric. Grelin liberally invokes the name of King Magni Bronzebeard to press for urgent action, an assertive tactic Senir notes is bound to agitate the stubborn Ironforge Senate. Senir admits he has fallen behind on filing his own observations due to the bitter cold, but receiving Grelin's dispatch nudges him back into service, opening further work monitoring hostile forces across the snowfields.
Why is Mountaineer Thalos having a traveler deliver the report?

Mountaineer Thalos is posted to hold the defense line at the Coldridge Valley tunnel against aggressive troggs. He cannot abandon his watchpost, so when an able adventurer comes through, he tasks them with carrying Grelin's dispatch safely into Kharanos.
why thalos asks you | thalos courier | who gives this quest

who is senir | senir whitebeard kharanos | senir background

The report compiles Grelin's findings on the Frostmane troll activity and incursions within Coldridge Valley. Written urgently, it invokes King Magni Bronzebeard's authority to demand reinforcements and attention from the authorities.

Mountaineer Thalos is stationed to guard the dangerous pass out of Coldridge Valley and cannot abandon his post. Grelin Whitebeard's reconnaissance on the trogg and troll threats is vital intelligence meant for his brother Senir, who coordinates broader defensive reports for Ironforge. Prove Your Worth is an introductory Horde quest offered by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To assist the Forsaken campaign against southern human and dwarven territories, adventurers are tasked with thinning the feral worgen prowling near the roadside. It marks the opening step in unraveling the arcane fallout wrought by Archmage Arugal.

Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, have set their sights on securing the regions south of Tirisfal Glades, including human and dwarven enclaves. However, the path through Silverpine Forest remains fraught with danger. Instead of an open staging ground, the Forsaken find their supply lines and forward bases threatened by feral Moonrage worgen that roam the pine-choked hills.

The presence of these beasts is no natural occurrence. Dalar Dawnweaver points the finger directly at Arugal, a disgraced former mage of Dalaran who unleashed otherworldly worgen upon the region during the Scourge invasion. Arugal has since claimed Shadowfang Keep, letting his feral creations overrun the forest. Before Dalar will entrust soldiers with deeper investigations into Arugal's sorcery, recruits must demonstrate their martial prowess by culling the nearest Moonrage Whitescalps.

Dalar Dawnweaver is a Forsaken mage stationed at the Sepulcher. He oversees efforts to counter the magical threats in Silverpine Forest, focusing primarily on neutralizing Archmage Arugal and his feral worgen pack.

Assigned by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, this quest tasks Forsaken agents with securing Arugal's earliest spellbooks from a nearby farmstead. Uncovering the magic behind the worgen curse is vital for the Forsaken to turn it against the mad mage and secure Silverpine Forest. Recovering the Remedy of Arugal marks the first step in unraveling the threat looming from Shadowfang Keep.

Dalar Dawnweaver, an ambitious Forsaken mage residing in the crypts of the Sepulcher, holds no respect for Archmage Arugal. To Dawnweaver, Arugal was an unremarkable practitioner whose inclusion in the Kirin Tor was baffling and whose magical understanding seemed amateurish. However, the monstrous beasts now roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver intends to deconstruct the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

Before seizing Shadowfang Keep, Arugal resided at a secluded wheat farm just north of the river bridge. Deathstalker scouts spotted discarded spellbooks preserved on the upper floor of the farmhouse, though lingering beasts prevented them from recovering the texts. Sifting through the dusty grimoires yields the incantation known as the Remedy of Arugal, revealing crucial insights into the unnatural curse spreading across Silverpine Forest.

Silverpine is the western shield of the Undercity. Reclaiming it from feral worgen is essential to securing the Dark Lady's borders.

This task sends Forsaken agents to collect enchanted shackles from Moonrage worgen roaming Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver, analyzing Arugal's notes, aims to unravel how the renegade mage artificially reinforced his unstable magic. Studying these bindings brings the Forsaken closer to dismantling the worgen threat plaguing the region.

Upon inspecting Arugal's recovered research, Dalar Dawnweaver expresses utter contempt for his former peer. According to Dalar, Arugal was never fit to serve Dalaran, let alone handle high sorcery during the kingdom's direst hour. To compensate for his mediocre talent, Arugal relied on enchanted relics and hardware to bolster and bind his summoned worgen beasts. Dalar requires physical samples of these items to dissect the magical tether holding the monsters together.

The cursed inhabitants of Silverpine, transformed into Moonrage worgen, wander the woods carrying physical manifestations of Arugal's binding enchantments. Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls stalk the regions to the north and east of the Sepulcher. Prized for the residual arcane energy woven into their metal, their heavy shackles serve as crucial specimens for Dawnweaver's counter-research against Shadowfang Keep.

Once summoned into this world by Arugal to repel the Scourge, the monstrous beasts quickly slipped from his control and overran the local lands. Bound by enchanted shackles that channel Arugal's crude magic, these corrupted predators now stalk the forest, terrorizing both surviving locals and Forsaken scouts traveling through the region.

Arugal's Folly is a key quest in the Sepulcher's ongoing campaign against the mad archmage's influence across Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver tasks Horde adventurers with infiltrating Deep Elem Mine to execute the corrupted foreman, Grimson the Pale, securing vital mineral wealth for Varimathras's forces.

While unraveling the dark enchantments Archmage Arugal unleashed upon the forest, Dalar Dawnweaver receives urgent intelligence from the Forsaken Darkstalkers. The feral sorcery spreading from Shadowfang Keep has reached the Deep Elem Mine in the southeastern hills, where worgen now make their lair. The mine holds crucial ore needed to fuel Undercity's militarization, but its current occupants render it completely unusable.

At the heart of the infested shafts lurks Grimson the Pale, the tainted foreman who directs the mad remnant within the subterranean tunnels. Dawnweaver orders an immediate decapitation strike: with Grimson slain and his head returned to the Sepulcher, the worgen in the shafts will lose their leader, allowing Forsaken laborers to claim the excavation for Lord Varimathras.

Grimson the Pale is the foreman of Deep Elem Mine. Like many laborers and residents in southern Silverpine, he fell under the corrupting magical influence radiating from Archmage Arugal's experiments, becoming a twisted figure overseeing an infested subterranean den.

Ivar the Foul is a quest in Silverpine Forest that marks the culmination of the reconnaissance mission undertaken by Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick. Trapped at the farmstead known as the Ivar Patch, Rane asks Horde travelers to eliminate the savage ghoul Ivar the Foul so Quinn can recover from his mauling and complete their report to High Executor Hadrec.

Siblings Rane and Quinn Yorick were deployed by the Deathstalkers to conduct reconnaissance across Silverpine Forest on behalf of High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their reconnaissance grinded to a sudden, violent halt when moving through a farmstead in the northern forest, where they were ambushed by the vicious ghoul known as Ivar the Foul.

Though the scouts managed to escape with their unlives, Quinn was severely mauled in the confrontation. Even after receiving an alchemical remedy concocted from forest beasts, Quinn remains too frail to march. Knowing Ivar prowls the nearby barn waiting for Rane's guard to falter, Rane calls upon Horde adventurers to storm the barn, sever Ivar's head, and permanently secure the homestead.

Ivar the Foul is a dangerous Scourge ghoul lingering in the northern reaches of Silverpine Forest. The Ivar Patch was once his own farm; he and most of his family and workers fell to the Scourge, and he now lurks there, ambushing passersby and savaging Forsaken scouts.
